uslaw-usc-t2-s661f:
Section 661f of Title 2 of the United States Code states the effect of credit reform on old law. The subchapter beats, shifts, or kills any prior law that clashes with it. That reach is cut off at laws passed before the 5th of November 1990. The text adds that no credit cap is set by the subchapter.

A second part deals with sums brought in from old loans. Loans bound or pledged before the 1st of October 1991 are the scope. Sums from them go to the winding-up accounts of federal agencies. Funds there may pay off the debts tied to those old loans. That use holds to the same reach the funds had before. Balances past current needs must be moved out of the accounts.
